base_member_text: [L468-L482] (MED/dimension validation) getarraydimsize_c checks only rank < dim, so dim values of zero or less can reach the SIZE intrinsic with an invalid dimension argument.
audit_member_text: [L454-L483] (HIGH/dimension-validation) Dimension-size lookup rejects only dim values greater than rank; zero or negative dimensions pass through and can reach SIZE with an invalid DIM argument, while rank-1 lookup ignores dim entirely.

adversarial.rationale: The exported function checks only array%rank < dim, and indextos validates the variable index, not DIM. Thus a valid rank-2 variable such as zb with dim=0 reaches SIZE with invalid DIM; the Python wrapper's +1 conversion does not protect direct C callers.

base_member_text: [L173-L180,L369-L376] (HIGH/unchecked index) The parameter-name and array-name entry points index keys or call indextos without validating the caller-supplied index, so an out-of-range C/API index can cause an out-of-bounds access.
audit_member_text: [L164-L180,L359-L376] (HIGH/bounds) Parameter and array name lookup index allocatable key/state tables directly without checking the caller-supplied index range.

adversarial.rationale: The parameter-name getter really indexes keys(index) unchecked, but the array-name getter delegates to indextos, which validates 1..numvars and halts before selecting storage. Retain the bounds finding only for getparametername_c.

base_member_text: [L454-L484] (MED/incorrect status contract) getarraydimsize_c initializes its function result to -1 and never changes it to success after computing dimsize, so every successful dimension query is reported as a failure.
audit_member_text: [L454-L484] (HIGH/status-contract) getarraydimsize_c initializes its status to -1 and never sets it to zero after successfully computing dimsize, so every call reports failure.

adversarial.rationale: After setting getarraydimsize_c=-1, every successful rank/type branch only assigns dimsize and falls through to the function end. The Fortran wrapper propagates this status, although the Python wrapper ignores it; no callee assignment changes the function result.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L145-L149] (MED/false success status) getparametertype_c unconditionally returns success and does not propagate whether getkey_indextype found the requested parameter.
audit_member_text: [L124-L149] (HIGH/error-propagation) getparametertype_c always returns success zero and does not validate the index returned by getkey_indextype, so an unknown parameter can return an undefined type code as a successful query.

adversarial.rationale: Unknown parameters do return success without checking index=-1, but the returned type code is deterministically blank rather than undefined. getkey_indextype initializes both outputs before searching, so retain only the misleading success-status defect.

base_member_text: [L587-L600,L635-L647,L682-L694,L730-L742,L820-L832,L868-L879] (MED/returned pointer lifetime) Each nonscalar C getter returns a pointer into a saved scratch allocation that is deallocated by the next call of the same rank/type, silently invalidating previously returned data and making the API non-reentrant.
audit_member_text: [L574-L743,L807-L881] (MED/pointer-lifetime) Array C getters return pointers into one saved scratch allocation per rank and deallocate that allocation on the next same-rank getter call, but this short lifetime is not exposed in the API.

adversarial.rationale: The scratch lifetime hazard affects direct native clients that retain a pointer across the next successful call to the same getter, separately for each rank and numeric type. The shipped Python wrapper copies non-scalar results into an ndarray before returning, so its previously returned arrays are not invalidated.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

audit_member_text: [L486-L507,L510-L1260] (MED/rank-type-validation) Generic and rank-specific array entry points validate only the mnemonic, not that the selected array's type and rank match the routine, before dereferencing a specific pointer component.

adversarial.rationale: Rank-specific getters/setters do select rN/iN after checking only the mnemonic, and the generated indextos code associates only the selected component. Exclude generic getarray from this specific claim: its arrayf2c callee in mnemoniciso.F90:32-45 returns an unrelated local scratch pointer rather than dereferencing a mismatched selected component.

audit_member_text: [L902-L1023,L1043-L1260] (HIGH/ffi/pointer-validation) All C array setters convert and dereference the incoming c_ptr without checking c_associated or receiving a buffer length, so null or undersized caller buffers cannot be rejected.

adversarial.rationale: Null or undersized buffers are unsafe for direct C setter calls with a valid mnemonic, but this is an invalid-caller-input robustness issue rather than a demonstrated failure with conforming buffers. base_member_text: [L529-L552,L764-L787] (HIGH/dangling C pointer) The scalar C getters return c_loc of an automatic local target (r0 or i0), whose lifetime ends when the function returns, leaving the caller with an invalid pointer.
audit_member_text: [L529-L552,L764-L787] (HIGH/dangling-pointer) Scalar C getters return c_loc of an unsaved local target, so the pointer becomes undefined as soon as the function returns.

adversarial.rationale: r0 and i0 are unsaved procedure-local TARGET scalars whose addresses escape at introspection.F90:550 and 785. The SAVE statement at module scope saves module variables, not these procedure locals, and the array metadata pointers do not extend the copied scalars' lifetimes.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

audit_member_text: [L130-L134,L386-L389,L416-L419,L448-L451] (HIGH/shape-conformance) Several Fortran wrappers assign the fixed 1024-element result of string_to_char_array into automatic arrays sized only len(name) or len(name)+1, which is a nonconforming whole-array assignment.

[L137-L149,L203-L223,L245-L269,L290-L311,L316-L336,L392-L406,L422-L436,L454-L505,L529-L1260] (HIGH/ffi/string-bounds) C entry points pass variable-length name arrays to char_array_to_string, whose dummy contract reads up to 1024 elements, so length-sized buffers without an in-range NUL can be read beyond their declared extent.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The C entry point declares only length elements but passes the array to the fixed-1024-element converter, whose strlen scans until a NUL. A length-sized buffer without a NUL is therefore read beyond its supplied extent; the Fortran wrappers also sometimes put the terminator at length+1, outside that declared extent.
